2607.19011.title: Computational Humor with Multimodal LLMs: Methods, Datasets, Evaluation, and Challenges
2607.19011.paper_summary: Multimodal humor in memes, cartoons, and comics remains difficult for AI systems because intended meaning depends on non-literal mechanisms, shared cultural knowledge, and communicative intent rather than literal scene description. This survey focuses on visual humor understanding in single-image and multi-panel artifacts, while treating humor generation as an emerging downstream frontier. We position the literature against prior humor, sarcasm, and general MLLM surveys and organize it using a capability-centric hierarchy spanning recognition, interpretation and reasoning, and generation. Under this lens, we synthesize benchmark design, evaluation protocols, and modeling paradigms, tracing the field's shift from task-specific fusion models to large-model approaches based on multimodal alignment, evidence-grounded reasoning, and controlled generation. We conclude by highlighting the main barriers to progress: shortcut-prone evaluation, limited cultural and narrative coverage, weak evidence grounding, and unresolved safety and ownership concerns.
2607.19011.paper_summary_zh: 多模態幽默在迷因、卡通和漫畫中對於 AI 系統來說仍然困難，因為預期的意義依賴於非字面機制、共享的文化知識和交流意圖，而不是字面場景描述。這項調查專注於單圖像和多面板作品中的視覺幽默理解，同時將幽默生成視為一個新興的下游前沿。我們將文獻與先前的幽默、諷刺和一般 MLLM 調查進行對比，並使用以能力為中心的層級結構進行組織，涵蓋識別、解釋和推理以及生成。在這個視角下，我們綜合了基準設計、評估協議和建模範式，追踪該領域從特定任務的融合模型轉向基於多模態對齊、證據基礎推理和受控生成的大型模型方法。我們最後強調了進展的主要障礙：易於走捷徑的評估、有限的文化和敘事覆蓋、薄弱的證據基礎，以及未解決的安全和所有權問題。
